transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I just don’t care about any of the things I used to love doing anymore—not fishing, not cooking, not even singing at church. Everything just feels completely empty to me now.
Can you tell me when you first started feeling this way and if it was triggered by a specific event or stressor in your life?

It all started about a year and a half ago when my wife passed away unexpectedly after a short hospital stay, which completely shattered my whole life and routine. Since then, this deep, heavy sadness and not caring about fishing or church has really taken hold, and it's been constant for a little over a year now.
Do you often find yourself feeling guilty about things that you think you could have done differently before your wife's passing, or do you blame yourself for her death in any way?

No, I don't really blame myself or feel guilty about her death, because it was just an unexpected medical event that happened so fast. It's more that since she's been gone, I just feel this overwhelming sadness and a deep emptiness that won't go away.

You mentioned feeling this deep sadness and emptiness for over a year now, can you tell me if these feelings have been consistently present every day since your wife's passing or have they waxed and waned over time?

It's been very consistent, honestly. Looking back over this past year and a half, I can only recall a few scattered days where I didn't feel completely weighed down and hopeless. From morning to night, that heavy, dark feeling is just hanging over me almost every single day.
Can you describe any activities or situations in the past year and a half where you have experienced even a slight sense of pleasure or enjoyment, no matter how brief?

No, I haven't felt any real pleasure or enjoyment at all over this past year and a half. Things that used to bring me so much joy—like grilling, singing gospel solos, or fixing things for neighbors—now just feel like chores I don't care about. I usually just end up sitting in my recliner, staring at the wall.
Have you experienced any significant changes in your appetite or sleep patterns since your wife's passing?

My appetite is pretty much gone, and I only really eat when my sister drops food off, though it just tastes like cardboard and my pants are hanging off me now. As for sleep, I mostly just lie awake in the dark with these heavy thoughts keeping me up.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy levels or movement, such as feeling slowed down or restless, since your wife's passing?

Lately, it feels like I’m moving through molasses—getting from my bed to the bathroom takes forever, and I’ll just sit on the edge of the bed staring at the floor for fifteen minutes before my body finally stands up. Other days, I'll completely freeze in place holding a dish, or pace back and forth rubbing my hands and muttering prayers because I can't get my body to do what makes sense.
Can you tell me more about these episodes where you feel like you're moving through molasses or freeze in place, and how often they happen?

These episodes have been happening almost every single day lately, or at least several times a week. It’s like my body just locks up and refuses to cooperate, whether I'm trying to get out of bed or just standing in the living room holding a tool. It takes so much effort just to make myself move, and I end up just staring at the floor or pacing and muttering prayers to try and get going.
Can you describe if there are any specific thoughts or emotions that trigger these episodes of feeling like you're moving through molasses or freezing in place?

There isn't really a specific thought or trigger that starts it, honestly. It just feels like a physical disconnect where my body refuses to obey my mind, or my head goes completely blank and heavy. I just get stuck or move incredibly slow without any warning.

Can you tell me if you've experienced any episodes of excessive and purposeless movement, like pacing back and forth, in addition to the episodes where you feel like you're moving through molasses or freezing in place?

Yes, I do pace back and forth quite a bit, rubbing my hands together and muttering little bits of prayers under my breath because I can't make my body do anything that makes sense. It's a strange feeling because it's the exact opposite of those times when I completely freeze in place or feel like I'm moving through molasses. I just feel so weary and overwhelmed, like my body is completely out of my control.

Can you tell me if you've noticed any periods where your symptoms, such as the feeling of moving through molasses or the episodes of pacing, have significantly improved or lifted, even if only for a short time, since your wife's passing?

There was a brief stretch late last summer when the heavy, sluggish feeling lifted slightly and I didn't feel quite as tearful or low. But even during those weeks, I was still convinced that folks from the church and the hospital were tracking me and sending me signs. Aside from that short time and a few scattered days, this heavy depression has been constant.
Can you tell me more about these feelings of being tracked by people from the church and the hospital, and if you've experienced any other unusual thoughts or perceptions since your wife's passing?

I keep thinking that people from the church and the hospital where my wife died are watching me and trying to punish me for something. When the mail is late or the TV screen flickers, I take it as a sign that they are keeping tabs on me and sending me messages. My sisters tell me it's crazy talk, but it feels so real to me and it just won't let up.
Can you describe in more detail these signs you believe you're receiving and how they relate to your feelings of being punished or tracked by others?

When the TV flickers, I feel like the hospital and church folks are sending coded signals to let me know they're watching my living room. If the mail is late, I'm convinced they've intercepted it to punish me for my wife's death, keeping tabs on everything I do. My sisters say it's just a coincidence, but it feels like a direct warning to me.
Can you tell me if you've ever heard voices or sounds that other people can't hear, or seen things that aren't really there, in addition to believing you're receiving these signs and being tracked?
No, I've never heard any voices or seen things that aren't really there. It's really just the feeling of being watched and those signs in the mail and on the TV that I've been experiencing.

Can you tell me more about how these beliefs of being tracked and receiving signs affect your daily life and interactions with others, and do you ever question whether these beliefs might not be true?

Believing they are keeping tabs on me has made me pull away from everyone, so I've stopped going to church and social gatherings just to stay safe at home. Even though my sisters tell me it's all "crazy talk," the signs feel too real and unsettling for me to doubt them, which just keeps me more isolated.
Do you think your beliefs about being tracked and receiving signs are possibly a result of your sadness and grief, or do you believe they are absolutely true and based on real events?

They started around the same time as the deep grief and sadness after losing my wife, so those feelings are definitely tangled together. But despite what my sisters tell me, the sense of being watched and receiving signs through the TV and mail feels completely real to me. It feels like an actual reality, not just something my mind is making up because I'm sad.

Can you describe how you differentiate between these signs and messages you believe you're receiving, and your own thoughts or feelings, and do you ever wonder if there could be another explanation for these events?

I'm not really sure how to explain how I tell them apart, to be honest. The signs just feel completely real and external to me when they happen, like they are happening right in front of my eyes. I haven't really thought about any other explanations because it just feels so certain in the moment.
Do you think it's possible that your feelings of being watched and receiving signs could be a part of your grief and sadness, rather than actual events happening to you?

The heavy sadness and the feeling of being watched did start around the same time, and they feel deeply tangled together. But even though my sisters call it "crazy talk," I still truly believe the late mail and flickering TV are real signs that they are keeping tabs on me. It feels completely real, rather than just being a product of my grief.

Can you tell me if you've ever had a moment, no matter how brief, where you questioned the reality of these signs and messages you believe you're receiving, or if you've considered the possibility that they might be a product of your own mind rather than actual events?

No, I haven't really had a moment of doubt because the signs feel completely real and solid when they happen. Even though my sisters keep telling me it's just "crazy talk," I truly believe the late mail and the flickering TV are actual messages they're sending me. I just haven't been able to see it as something that's only in my head.

Do you think it's possible that your belief in being tracked and receiving signs could be related to the same feelings of sadness and grief that have been affecting you since your wife's passing, rather than being based on real events or messages from others?

The heavy sadness and the feeling of being watched are definitely deeply tangled together, and they both started right after my wife passed. But even if it is connected to my grief, those signs and the feeling of being watched still feel completely real and unsettling to me. No matter what others say, I just can't shake the feeling that they are actually keeping tabs on me.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts are being controlled or influenced by an external force, or that you're being forced to think certain thoughts against your will?

No, I've never felt like my actual thoughts are being controlled or that anyone is putting thoughts into my head. It's more that I feel like they are watching me from the outside and sending me messages through the TV and the mail. My own thoughts still feel like my own.
Can you tell me if you have ever had a moment where you felt like your beliefs about being tracked and receiving signs were not true, or if you have always been completely convinced of their reality?

I have always been completely convinced that it is real, and I've never really had a single moment of doubt. Even though my sisters keep telling me it's just "crazy talk," when the TV flickers or the mail is late, it feels 100% real to me. I just can't shake the feeling that they are actually keeping tabs on me.
Do you think that if you were to feel better and your sadness were to lift, you would still believe that people from the church and hospital are tracking you and sending you signs?

Yes, I believe I would still feel that way, because I actually had a period late last summer when my mood lifted slightly and I wasn't feeling as deeply depressed or tearful. Even during those weeks when the heavy sadness wasn't there, I was still completely convinced that the people from the church and the hospital were tracking me and sending me signs.
Can you tell me if you think your feelings of being watched and receiving signs would still be present if your sadness and depression were to completely go away?

Yes, I believe they would still be present. Like I mentioned, during that stretch late last summer when I didn't feel nearly as low or deeply depressed, I was still completely convinced that the church and hospital folks were tracking me and sending me signs. That feeling of being watched didn't go away just because my mood had lifted for a bit.

You mentioned that even when your mood slightly improved last summer, you still believed people were tracking you and sending signs. Do you think this belief is something that could be changed by anything, or do you feel it's an absolute truth that won't change regardless of how you're feeling?

It feels like an absolute truth to me, and I don't think anything could change that because it's what is actually happening. Even when my sisters try to convince me it's just "crazy talk" and that I'm wrong, I just can't shake the feeling that it's real. No matter if my mood is deeply depressed or a bit better, things like the flickering TV and the late mail still feel like solid proof that I'm being watched and targeted.

Can you tell me if you think there's any possibility, no matter how small, that your beliefs about being tracked and receiving signs might not be based on real events, but rather on your own thoughts and feelings?

My sisters keep telling me it's just "crazy talk" and that it's all in my head, but to me, it feels completely real and unsettling. When the TV flickers or the mail is late, it genuinely feels like a direct message, making it very difficult to just dismiss it as my own thoughts, even if I wish I could.
Do you think your beliefs about being tracked and receiving signs are part of your sadness and grief, or do you believe they are separate and unrelated to your emotional state?

Most of the time, the heavy sadness and the feeling of being watched feel deeply tangled together, since they both started around the same time after my wife passed. However, during that stretch late last summer, my deep depression lifted a bit but I still felt strongly that people were tracking me and sending signs. Because of that, I think they might not be entirely the same thing, even if they usually go hand in hand.

Can you tell me if you think your belief in being tracked and receiving signs would still be present if you were no longer feeling sad or depressed, or if it would go away along with your other symptoms?

Yes, I truly believe those thoughts would still be there even if the sadness went away completely. During that stretch late last summer when I wasn't feeling deeply depressed or tearful, I was still completely convinced that the church and hospital folks were tracking me and sending me signs. It just feels like a separate reality that doesn't go away when my mood improves.
Can you tell me if you think these signs and messages you believe you're receiving could be a part of a larger pattern of distorted thinking that's affecting your perception of reality?

I don't know, it's all so confusing because when the TV flickers it feels completely real, but my sisters keep calling it "crazy talk" and I wonder if my mind is playing tricks on me. I just get so lost thinking about how I used to fix things around the neighborhood before my wife died, and now my head is just foggy and jumping all over. It is just so exhausting to live like this every single day.
Do you think that if you were completely cured of your depression and sadness, you would still believe that people from the church and hospital are tracking you and sending you signs?

Yes, I do think I would still believe it because those thoughts seem to exist separate from my sadness. Late last summer, there was a stretch of time where I didn't feel as deeply depressed or tearful, yet I was still completely convinced that the people from the church and the hospital were tracking me and sending me signs. It just feels like that tracking has a life of its own, regardless of how low my mood is.
